title: Line up a motor's belt pulley with a blower's pulley using a straightedge
instruction: Line up the motor's pulley with the blower's pulley. Slide and turn the loose motor on its base plate, keeping it on the plate and the same distance from the blower, until its pulley's outer face is in the same plane as the blower pulley's outer face, so the straightedge laid across both faces touches each pulley at both rims. Then let go of the motor and the straightedge and move both grippers away.
context: Belt-drive air handlers, rooftop units and exhaust fans have a motor on an adjustable base driving the fan through V-belts. After a motor is replaced or its base is moved, HVAC mechanics line the motor's pulley (sheave) up with the fan's before the belts go on: a straightedge, often a strip of extruded aluminium, laid across both pulleys' outer faces should touch each pulley at both rims. Gates' alignment guidance limits a V-belt drive's total misalignment, angular and parallel added together, to 1/2 degree (about 1/10 inch per foot), and notes that misalignment wears and fatigues belts and can destroy one in hours or days. Here the fixed pulley is 29 cm from the motor's, so the straightedge has to be held flat on it while the motor is brought into line. Done by: HVAC mechanics and installers (O*NET 49-9021.00), maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00).
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Blower, fixed, dark grey painted steel: a housing box 120 mm along x, 100 mm along y and 140 mm tall standing on the table at x 27.0 to 39.0 cm, y -20.0 to -10.0 cm; from its front face (toward the arms) a 16 mm grey steel shaft runs 20 mm along -x, its axis 52 mm above the table at y -15.0 cm, carrying a black cast-iron pulley 90 mm across and 20 mm thick (x 23.0 to 25.0 cm, its bottom 7 mm above the table). The pulley's outer face, toward the arms, is the line x 23.0 cm. (2) Motor base plate, fixed: light grey galvanised steel, 160 mm along x, 130 mm along y, 12 mm thick, on the table at x 26.2 to 42.2 cm, y 7.5 to 20.5 cm. (3) Motor, loose, 150 g in all (a bench model: a blue 3D-printed shell, a grey steel shaft, a black printed pulley): a body box 90 mm long, 70 mm wide and 80 mm tall; from the middle of one end face a 16 mm shaft 25 mm long, then a pulley 64 mm across and 18 mm thick. Its mass is spread evenly through its volume: the centre of mass is 40 mm above the body's underside, 9 mm from the body's centre toward the pulley. The shaft's axis is 40 mm above the body's underside (52 mm above the table: level with the blower's); the pulley's outer face is 88 mm from the body's centre and its bottom 8 mm above the body's underside. The motor stands on the plate, the centre of the body's underside at x 33.0 cm, y 14.0 cm, its shaft pointing toward the arms, turned 3 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from square: the centre of its pulley's outer face is at x 24.21 cm, 12.1 mm behind the line. (4) Straightedge, loose: a bare silver aluminium box section 20 x 40 mm with 1.2 mm walls, 480 mm long, 180 g, standing on a 20 mm face (40 mm tall) on the felt, its length along y, its centre at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm (it spans y -28.5 to +19.5 cm). (5) Felt strip, fixed: green felt 40 mm along x, 500 mm along y, 2 mm thick, under the straightedge, centred at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm. The pulleys' centres are 290 mm apart (y -15.0 and +14.0 cm). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial from the motor's pose and both grippers. F is the centre of the motor pulley's outer face; e is how far F is behind (+) or in front of (-) the line x 23.0 cm, the blower pulley's outer face; theta is the motor's turn about the vertical from square, signed and never folded (a motor turned round is 180 degrees out); alpha = atan(|e| / 290 mm), the offset as an angle over the centre distance. Total misalignment M = |theta| + alpha, in degrees: angular plus parallel, added as the belt maker adds them. Score 0 unless all five hold: (a) at rest: over the last 0.5 s F moved less than 2 mm in all and the motor turned less than 0.5 degree in all; (b) upright: the body's up axis within 2 degrees of vertical; (c) on its plate: all four bottom corners of the body inside the plate's outline and within 2 mm of its top; (d) on its line: the centre of the body's underside within 10 mm of y 14.0 cm (keeping the 290 mm centre distance); (e) hands off: each gripper's tool centre point and pad-tip point at least 60 mm from the motor's and the straightedge's bounding boxes (a fully open finger reaches 57 mm out, so open fingers left resting on either fail too). If the grippers cannot be read on a step, (e) counts as met there (counted in the trace). With all five: 1.0 if M <= 0.5 degree (the V-belt limit: an offset alone up to 2.53 mm, or a turn alone up to 0.5 degree, 0.56 mm across the 64 mm pulley); 0.5 if M <= 1.0 degree (5.06 mm alone); 0.25 if M <= 2.0 degrees (10.1 mm alone); else 0. At the start M is 5.39 degrees (e +12.1 mm, theta 3 degrees): 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0; every end state has exactly one: 0 if a gate fails, else the band M is in. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Holding the motor in line or the straightedge against it fails (e); sliding the motor along y to change the centre distance fails (d); turning it round fails through theta; tipping it or lifting it off the plate fails (b) or (c); pushing it past the line costs through e. In a real trial: tape a line on the table along y at x 20.0 cm, 30 mm in front of the blower pulley's face; stand a try-square on the table with its blade against the motor pulley's face at each rim at the shaft's height (64 mm apart) and read each one's distance from the tape with a steel rule, d1 and d2: e = (d1 + d2)/2 - 30 mm, theta = asin(|d1 - d2| / 64 mm). With the motor not proud, the straightedge laid flat on the blower pulley's face gives the same with a feeler gauge: e = (g1 + g2)/2 and theta = asin(|g1 - g2| / 64 mm) from the gaps at the motor pulley's two rims. A photo shows the motor upright on its plate within 10 mm of a taped y mark and both grippers clear.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, uniform friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The blower is one fixed compound and the motor one loose rigid body (150 g, a bench model; a real motor is heavier and takes more push). No belt: it goes on after aligning. The pulleys' groove-to-face thicknesses are equal, so face alignment is groove alignment; the shafts are level by construction, so only the motor's slide and turn on its plate are scored (no twist). No base bolts or slots.
reset_notes: Put the motor back on its plate: the centre of its body's underside at x 33.0 cm, y 14.0 cm, turned 3 degrees anticlockwise (seen from above) from square, its pulley face 12.1 mm behind the line. Stand the straightedge back on its 20 mm face on the felt, along y, centred at x 15.0 cm, y -4.5 cm. The blower, the plate and the felt are fixed; nothing is consumed.
